newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end floor trade little changed.
newsitem.headline: German shares end floor trade little changed.

text.p: German shares ended floor trade little changed in quiet dealings on Monday after recovering from early losses brought on by the dollar's sharp decline in Asian dealings.

The 30-share DAX index ended up 0.12 points at 3,184.21 after falling as low as 3.175.96 earlier in the session. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 18.86 points at 3,184.93 by 1310 GMT.
Traders generally expected the market to remain stable ahead of Greenspan's testimony to the U.S. Congress on Wednesday and Thursday.
"This development is healthy," one share dealer said. "If the bond markets don't go mad shares should soon find their feet again."
Attention will be fixed on what Greenspan has to say about U.S. stock market market activity, especially since previous comments about the market briefly interrupted the advance.

The biggest mover among DAX stocks was steel and engineering group Thyssen AG, which ended floor trade up 14 marks or 4.4 percent at 332.50 marks after Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said it had raised the stock to overweight from neutral.
Deutsche MG also said it expected the shares to hit 400 marks over the next year or two.

Dollar-sensitive chemical and engineering companies were under most pressure from the decline in the dollar, which fell more than a pfennig against the mark as low as 1.6738 marks in late Tokyo trade on Monday but which edged up to 1.6750-60 marks by 1310 GMT in European trade.
Shares in chemicals group Hoechst AG fell 1.60 marks to 70.25 marks.
